source_name: NBS – Inštitúcie elektronických peňazí (e-money institutions supervision & register)
why_relevant: NBS supervises and maintains the list of Slovak EMIs; the section carries licensing conditions and the authoritative national register — the entry gate for e-money business in SK.

source_name: NBS – Platobné inštitúcie a AISP: postup podania žiadosti / pred podaním žiadosti
why_relevant: Procedural rules for PI/PISP authorisation and AISP registration in SK, including the pre-application channel (psd2@nbs.sk) and the requirement of SK head office. Directly governs market entry conditions for payment providers.

source_name: NBS – Príručka pre prípravu žiadosti o udelenie povolenia (licensing application handbook, PDF)
why_relevant: Detailed NBS expectations for PI/EMI licence files (business model, capital, governance, outsourcing). Useful as a proxy for supervisory priorities and for benchmarking entry effort.

source_name: NBS aktuality – news on opening SIPS/TARGET-SK to non-bank PSPs
why_relevant: Announces that from 6 Oct 2025 PIs and EMIs may apply to participate directly in SIPS or TARGET-SK — a structural change in SK payment-market access, and a leading indicator of new direct participants.

source_name: European Payments Council – SCT Inst rulebook & implementation guidelines
why_relevant: The scheme rulebook that binds SK PSPs contractually rather than by national law: 2025 SCT Inst v1.1 in force to 21 Nov 2027, 5/7/9-second timing rules, structured-address migration (Nov 2026). These deadlines never appear in Slovak legislation.

source_name: European Payments Council – Verification of Payee (VOP) scheme rulebook & EPC Directory Service
why_relevant: VOP rulebook in force since 5 Oct 2025; all SCT/SCT Inst participants must adhere and fund the EDS for an initial 3 years. Directly determines SK PSP obligations and vendor (RVM) demand.

source_name: EPC Register of Participants (SEPA scheme adherence lists)
why_relevant: Adherence registers show which SK PSPs (and which RVMs serving them) are live in SCT, SCT Inst and VOP — the best objective indicator of Slovak scheme readiness and of vendor footprints.

source_name: EBA central register of payment and electronic money institutions (PSD2)
why_relevant: EU-wide, daily-updated, downloadable register fed by NBS. Gives a machine-readable view of SK PIs/EMIs/PISPs/AISPs plus inbound passporting into Slovakia — better for time-series than the NBS HTML lists.

source_name: Slov-Lex – zákon č. 492/2009 Z. z. o platobných službách (consolidated text & amendment history)
why_relevant: The national statute governing payment services, PI/EMI licensing and payment systems in SK (transposing PSD2; future home of PSD3/PSR alignment). Slov-Lex gives consolidated versions and effective dates.

source_name: Slov-Lex portál právnych predpisov – legislatívny proces (PK / medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie)
why_relevant: The SK inter-ministerial consultation module is where MF SR drafts amending the payments law first surface, with comment deadlines — the earliest formal signal of upcoming SK payments regulation.

source_name: NR SR (Slovak Parliament) document repository – payments bills and explanatory memoranda
why_relevant: Parliamentary texts and dôvodové správy for the payment services act reveal intent, transition periods and derogations that the consolidated law text hides.

source_name: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (public rulebook PDF)
why_relevant: Card scheme rulebook binding SK issuers/acquirers; carries dated mandates (e.g. subscription-management/cardholder-control requirements from 18 Apr 2026, enhanced merchant data 23 Jan 2027) that never appear in national law.

source_name: Mastercard Rules portal (Mastercard Rules manuals)
why_relevant: Counterpart scheme rulebook for SK acquirers/issuers and processors; public manuals give the rule baseline, while release bulletins with the actual mandate deadlines sit behind Mastercard Connect.

source_name: ECB – oversight of payment instruments/schemes (PISA framework) and card payment oversight consultations
why_relevant: ECB/Eurosystem oversight sets scheme-level expectations that NBS applies nationally; consultations here precede requirements later imposed on SK schemes and PSPs.

source_name: EUR-Lex – SK-language texts of payments regulations (IPR 2024/886, SEPA 260/2012, SFD 98/26/ES)
why_relevant: Authoritative Slovak-language versions of the EU acts that bind SK PSPs directly (instant payments, SEPA end-dates, settlement finality). Also disambiguates 'SIPS' the ECB SIPS Regulation from SIPS the Slovak system.

source_name: Podnikajte.sk – practitioner coverage of SK payment obligations (instant payments, VOP)
why_relevant: Business-press explainers translate scheme/EU deadlines into how SK banks actually implement them; useful for detecting divergence between formal deadlines and practice, and for naming banks.

source_name: Slovak bank payment-service pages as de-facto implementation evidence (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa platobný styk)
why_relevant: Bank product/T&C pages reveal actual go-live dates, limits and cut-off times for instant payments and VOP in SK — the observable end state of scheme rulebook adoption.

source_name: NBS – Subjekty finančného trhu (database of supervised financial market entities)
why_relevant: Master NBS database enumerating every supervised entity in SK by sector (banks, branches of foreign banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, limited payment service providers, payment agents, crypto-asset service providers, funds, insurers). This is the canonical map of actors from which all actor-level sources are discovered, and it reflects new authorisations and revocations.

source_name: NBS – Register podľa PSD2 (PSD2 register of payment service providers and agents)
why_relevant: National PSD2 register: authorised payment institutions, e-money institutions, AISPs, limited-scope providers and their agents/branches. Core actor list for the payments workstream and the feed that populates the EBA central register for SK.

source_name: NBS – Platobné inštitúcie a AISP (payment institutions and AISPs section)
why_relevant: Supervisory landing page for PI/AISP licensing: application requirements, forms, notification duties, and links to the entity lists. Useful for spotting licensing-process changes and deadlines.

source_name: registre.nbs.sk – NBS register portal (professional competence, other registers)
why_relevant: Dedicated NBS registers portal hosting sub-registers (odborná spôsobilosť for institutions and persons, and others). Search results indicate daily refresh from source databases (~05:00, regenerated hourly), which makes it usable as a change-detection feed.

source_name: regfap.nbs.sk – Register finančných agentov a finančných poradcov
why_relevant: Statutory register of financial agents and financial advisors (distribution layer for banking/insurance/payment products). Enumerates thousands of intermediary actors and their sectoral scope — key for channel/partner mapping.

source_name: regver.nbs.sk – Register veriteľov (register of consumer-credit creditors)
why_relevant: Register of licensed non-bank consumer-credit providers ('nebankovky'). Enumerates lending competitors outside the bank perimeter and flags licence withdrawals.

source_name: NBS – Zoznam registrov údajov o spotrebiteľských úveroch (list of consumer-credit data registers)
why_relevant: Points to the recognised private credit-bureau registers operating in SK (a second tier of data infrastructure actors beyond NBS itself).

source_name: NBS – Register bankových úverov a záruk (RBUZ)
why_relevant: Statutory credit register run by NBS; the page documents reporting obligations and participants, which indirectly identifies every reporting credit institution and the data-submission deadlines they face.

source_name: NBS – Centrálna evidencia regulovaných informácií (CERI)
why_relevant: Slovak OAM: central store of regulated disclosures by issuers (including listed banks). Source of mandatory corporate disclosures tied to statutory deadlines.

source_name: NBS – Kryptoaktíva: udelenie povolenia / dohľad (MiCA CASP licensing and list)
why_relevant: MiCA authorisation pipeline and the resulting list of licensed crypto-asset service providers in SK (a small, fast-moving new licence class; NBS reported six licensed CASPs). Direct evidence of new entrants into the SK payments/crypto perimeter.

source_name: EBA – Credit Institutions Register (CIR)
why_relevant: EU-wide authoritative list of authorised credit institutions including SK entities, downloadable in bulk. Enables cross-border comparison and detects SK banks' authorisations/withdrawals in a standardised schema.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision – List of supervised entities (SI/LSI)
why_relevant: SSM list identifying which SK banks are significant institutions supervised directly by the ECB vs less significant under NBS. Determines which supervisor's consultations and deadlines apply to each SK bank.
